title: Bollobás–Erdős–Tuza Conjecture (Conjecture 1.1)
statement_text: For every real $\delta>0$, every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G)\geq\delta|V(G)|$ satisfies $\eta(G)\leq o(|V(G)|)$.
context_text: Bollobás, Erdős and Tuza raised this conjecture asserting that any graph with a stable set larger than a constant fraction of the vertex set has a hitting set of all maximum stable sets that is sublinear in the number of vertices. The conjecture is still open; Hajnal proved it for $\delta>1/2$, and Alon provided constructions showing $\eta(G)$ can be arbitrarily large even when $\alpha(G)$ is linear in $|V(G)|$.
paper_contribution: The paper introduces the $\eta$-boundedness framework as a structured approach to this conjecture, and proves $\eta$-boundedness for several hereditary graph classes (including $P_5$-free graphs of bounded clique number), contributing indirectly to the study of Conjecture 1.1 for graphs of bounded chromatic number.
paper_title: Hitting all maximum stable sets in $P_5$-free graphs

title: Conjecture 1.8
statement_text: For every forest $H$, there exists a function $f:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{N}$ such that every $H$-free graph $G$ satisfies $\eta(G)\leq f(\omega(G))$.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; $H$-free means with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$. A hitting set of $G$ is a set of vertices meeting every maximum stable set of $G$ (equivalently, whose removal decreases $\alpha(G)$), and $\eta(G)$ is the minimum size of a hitting set. A class $\mathcal{C}$ is $\eta$-bounded if there is $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $\eta(G)\le f(\omega(G))$ for all $G\in\mathcal{C}$, and polynomially $\eta$-bounded if moreover $f(x)=x^d$ for some $d\in\mathbb{N}$. The notion parallels $\chi$-boundedness: $G$ is perfect if and only if $\eta(H)\le\omega(H)$ for every induced subgraph $H$ of $G$, there are graphs with arbitrarily large girth and $\eta$, and every hereditary polynomially $\eta$-bounded class satisfies the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture. This conjecture is proposed as the analogue of the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture for $\eta$-boundedness, motivated by the existence of graphs with large girth and large $\eta$. It holds easily for stars ($K_{1,s}$-free graphs satisfy $\eta(G)\le\omega(G)^s$, because a vertex of degree $d$ yields a hitting set of size $d+1$) and for induced subgraphs of $P_4$ ($P_4$-free graphs are perfect). The authors prove it for $P_5$, for every graph $H$ having a vertex incident with all its edges (e.g. disjoint unions of a star and isolated vertices), and for trees obtained from a star by subdividing at most one edge once; it remains open even for trees of diameter three, for $P_6$, and for the disjoint union of two stars. They also propose the stronger polynomial version (for every forest $H$ there is $d$ with $\eta(G)\le\omega(G)^d$ for $H$-free $G$).

title: Conjecture 1.13
statement_text: For every integer $t\geq 6$, the class of $P_{t}$-free graphs is $\eta$-bounded.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; $H$-free means with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$. A hitting set of $G$ is a set of vertices meeting every maximum stable set of $G$ (equivalently, whose removal decreases $\alpha(G)$), and $\eta(G)$ is the minimum size of a hitting set. A class $\mathcal{C}$ is $\eta$-bounded if there is $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $\eta(G)\le f(\omega(G))$ for all $G\in\mathcal{C}$, and polynomially $\eta$-bounded if moreover $f(x)=x^d$ for some $d\in\mathbb{N}$. The notion parallels $\chi$-boundedness: $G$ is perfect if and only if $\eta(H)\le\omega(H)$ for every induced subgraph $H$ of $G$, there are graphs with arbitrarily large girth and $\eta$, and every hereditary polynomially $\eta$-bounded class satisfies the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture. The authors conjecture, as an analogue of the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture, that for every forest $H$ the $H$-free graphs are $\eta$-bounded; this is easy for stars ($K_{1,s}$-free graphs satisfy $\eta(G)\le\omega(G)^s$, since a vertex of degree $d$ gives $\eta\le d+1$) and for induced subgraphs of $P_4$ (perfect graphs). The main result of the paper is that $P_5$-free graphs are $\eta$-bounded, with a proof much longer than the classical Gyárfás path argument that gives $\chi$-boundedness of $P_t$-free graphs for every $t$ (the bound obtained is super-exponential). Whether $P_t$-free graphs are $\eta$-bounded for $t\ge6$ remains open.

title: Conjecture 1.16
statement_text: For every forest $H$, there exists $d\in\mathbb{N}$ such that every $H$-free graph $G$ satisfies $\eta(G)\leq\omega(G)^{d}$.
context_text: A polynomial strengthening of Conjecture 1.8, proposed in connection with the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture. The authors note that the analogous polynomial strengthening of the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture is also open, and that there exist $\chi$-bounded classes that are not polynomially $\chi$-bounded.

title: Conjecture 1.17
statement_text: There exists $d\in\mathbb{N}$ such that every $P_{5}$-free graph $G$ satisfies $\eta(G)\leq\omega(G)^{d}$.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; $H$-free means with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$. A hitting set of $G$ is a set of vertices meeting every maximum stable set of $G$ (equivalently, whose removal decreases $\alpha(G)$), and $\eta(G)$ is the minimum size of a hitting set. A class $\mathcal{C}$ is $\eta$-bounded if there is $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $\eta(G)\le f(\omega(G))$ for all $G\in\mathcal{C}$, and polynomially $\eta$-bounded if moreover $f(x)=x^d$ for some $d\in\mathbb{N}$. The notion parallels $\chi$-boundedness: $G$ is perfect if and only if $\eta(H)\le\omega(H)$ for every induced subgraph $H$ of $G$, there are graphs with arbitrarily large girth and $\eta$, and every hereditary polynomially $\eta$-bounded class satisfies the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture. The authors prove that $P_5$-free graphs are $\eta$-bounded, but with a super-exponential bound (they say it would be interesting even to obtain a singly exponential bound), and that $H$-free graphs are polynomially $\eta$-bounded whenever $H$ is a proper induced subgraph of $P_5$. This conjecture is the $P_5$ case of their conjecture that $H$-free graphs are polynomially $\eta$-bounded for every forest $H$; it is singled out because, by the Erdős–Hajnal connection above, it would imply the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture for $P_5$-free graphs.

title: Conjecture 1.20
statement_text: For every integer $t\geq 3$, $M_{t}$-free graphs are polynomially $\eta$-bounded.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; $H$-free means with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$. A hitting set of $G$ is a set of vertices meeting every maximum stable set of $G$ (equivalently, whose removal decreases $\alpha(G)$), and $\eta(G)$ is the minimum size of a hitting set. A class $\mathcal{C}$ is $\eta$-bounded if there is $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $\eta(G)\le f(\omega(G))$ for all $G\in\mathcal{C}$, and polynomially $\eta$-bounded if moreover $f(x)=x^d$ for some $d\in\mathbb{N}$. The notion parallels $\chi$-boundedness: $G$ is perfect if and only if $\eta(H)\le\omega(H)$ for every induced subgraph $H$ of $G$, there are graphs with arbitrarily large girth and $\eta$, and every hereditary polynomially $\eta$-bounded class satisfies the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture. $M_t$ denotes the $1$-regular graph on $2t$ vertices, i.e. a matching of $t$ edges (so $M_t$-free means no induced matching of size $t$). The authors prove that $H$-free graphs are polynomially $\eta$-bounded whenever $H$ has maximum degree at most one and at most four vertices of degree one (this covers $M_2$, an induced subgraph of $P_5$). They conjecture this natural strengthening for all $t$, although, strikingly, it is not even known whether $M_3$-free graphs are $\eta$-bounded.

title: Open problem on $\eta$-boundedness for disjoint union of two stars
statement_text: It remains open whether the disjoint union of two stars satisfies the $\eta$-analogue of the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture, i.e. whether the class of $(S_{a}\cup S_{b})$-free graphs is $\eta$-bounded for all $a,b\geq 1$, where $S_a$ denotes the star $K_{1,a}$.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; $H$-free means with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$. A hitting set of $G$ is a set of vertices meeting every maximum stable set of $G$ (equivalently, whose removal decreases $\alpha(G)$), and $\eta(G)$ is the minimum size of a hitting set. A class $\mathcal{C}$ is $\eta$-bounded if there is $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $\eta(G)\le f(\omega(G))$ for all $G\in\mathcal{C}$, and polynomially $\eta$-bounded if moreover $f(x)=x^d$ for some $d\in\mathbb{N}$. The notion parallels $\chi$-boundedness: $G$ is perfect if and only if $\eta(H)\le\omega(H)$ for every induced subgraph $H$ of $G$, there are graphs with arbitrarily large girth and $\eta$, and every hereditary polynomially $\eta$-bounded class satisfies the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture. The authors conjecture, as an analogue of the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture, that for every forest $H$ the $H$-free graphs are $\eta$-bounded; this is easy for stars ($K_{1,s}$-free graphs satisfy $\eta(G)\le\omega(G)^s$, since a vertex of degree $d$ gives $\eta\le d+1$) and for induced subgraphs of $P_4$ (perfect graphs). For $\chi$-boundedness it is straightforward that a forest satisfies the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture if and only if all its components do; the authors do not know whether the analogous statement holds for $\eta$-boundedness, and in particular whether the disjoint union of two stars satisfies it. As a weakening they prove that $H$-free graphs are $\eta$-bounded whenever $H$ has a vertex incident with all edges of $H$ (a star plus isolated vertices).
